g10-geography-ug8-t1.overview: Basic Concepts of Geospatial Information sits inside Geospatial Information and Data Processing. Geospatial information is the focus of Unit 8 of Grade 10 Geography in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it separates data from information and defines geospatial data by place, time, and attributes. Then it explains how geographers gather data directly and through remote sensing, using tools like GPS and digitizers. Next, it describes how maps show features as points, lines, and areas in vector and raster form. Also it traces mapmaking from cave paintings to the geographic information system and its components. Finally, it shows how to build bar graphs, line graphs, pie charts, and diagrams from raw data. Students will also learn how geospatial information applies to real-life situations, such as planning, mapping, and research.
objectives: Explain the difference between data and geospatial information.
Describe the sources and tools of geographic data.
Identify how maps show points, lines, and areas.
Compare vector and raster data models.
Describe the components and uses of a geographic information system.
g10-geography-ug8-t1.simple:
Basic Concepts of Geospatial Information in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the difference between raw data and processed information.
  • The data lifecycle of collecting, processing, analyzing, and sharing.
  • Also geospatial data as location, attribute, and temporal information.
  • Discrete objects and continuous fields as two ways to picture the world.
g10-geography-ug8-t1.detailed:
Basic Concepts of Geospatial Information — the essentials. First, the difference between raw data and processed information. The data lifecycle of collecting, processing, analyzing, and sharing. Also geospatial data as location, attribute, and temporal information. Discrete objects and continuous fields as two ways to picture the world.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Explain the difference between data and geospatial information.
  • Describe the sources and tools of geographic data.
  • Identify how maps show points, lines, and areas.
  • Compare vector and raster data models.
  • Describe the components and uses of a geographic information system.
